implementation_notes: The JDK supplies the structure: ConcurrentLinkedQueue is an unbounded MPMC queue documented as an efficient non-blocking algorithm based on Michael & Scott's paper, so application code calls offer()/poll() and never writes the CAS loop, with documented happens-before effects on publication and removal. It never blocks and never fails, which also means no backpressure and busy polling: for waiting consumers use LinkedTransferQueue (take()/transfer()) or a lock-based BlockingQueue. size() is not constant-time, so keep a separate atomic counter if one is needed, and never use isEmpty() as a synchronisation point.
pitfalls: Unbounded by design: a producer that outruns consumers grows the heap; there is no full() and offer() never fails.
poll() in a loop is a spin - pair it with park/unpark, a semaphore, or switch to LinkedTransferQueue/BlockingQueue when a consumer must wait.
size(), isEmpty() and iterators are weakly consistent or O(n) traversals and must not drive control flow.

variants.name: LinkedTransferQueue (transfer / rendezvous)
variants.implementation_notes: LinkedTransferQueue is the JDK's linked TransferQueue: transfer(e) waits until a consumer receives the element, tryTransfer(e) succeeds only if a consumer is already waiting, and take() blocks the caller until an element arrives. Use it when the hand-off itself is the synchronisation - a producer that should deliver work to a waiting worker rather than dropping it into a buffer - while ConcurrentLinkedQueue stays the simpler choice for plain buffering.
pitfalls: transfer() blocks and is interruptible: it is a lock-free queue with a parking path, not a non-blocking producer.
hasWaitingConsumer()/getWaitingConsumerCount() are estimates, so admission control must not depend on them.
